subject: Vocabulary
description: High-frequency phrasal verbs from SSC, banking, RRB PYQ

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'CALL OFF': 'The match was called off due to rain.'

options.option_text: Postponed to a later date possibly

questions.explanation: CALL OFF = cancel / abandon (esp. an event already planned). 'Call off the wedding', 'call off the strike'. Note distinction: CALL OFF = cancel (not happening at all). POSTPONE = delay to a later date (will happen later). PUT OFF = postpone (also delay something disliked). CALL OUT = challenge or summon publicly.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'BEAR OUT': 'The data bears out our hypothesis.'

options.option_text: Hides or conceals the truth from

questions.explanation: BEAR OUT = support, confirm, prove correct. 'The witness bore out my story' = backed it up. Note other 'bear' phrasals: BEAR DOWN = press down on; BEAR UP = endure (under hardship); BEAR ON = be relevant to; BEAR WITH = be patient with. PYQ-favourite phrasal.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'GO THROUGH': 'I went through the report carefully.'

options.option_text: Tear up and throw away aside

questions.explanation: GO THROUGH = examine, read, study carefully OR endure (a difficult experience). 'Go through the document' = read carefully. 'Go through hardship' = experience hardship. Other GO phrasals: GO OVER = review; GO ON = continue; GO AHEAD = proceed; GO BACK = return; GO INTO = enter or examine in detail.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'KEEP AT': 'You must keep at it to succeed.'

options.option_text: Avoid the task at all costs
Persist with effort, not giving up

questions.explanation: KEEP AT (something) = persist; continue working at; not give up. 'Keep at it!' = encouragement to persist. KEEP UP = maintain pace, continue at same level. KEEP OUT = stay out / exclude. KEEP AWAY = stay distant. KEEP ON = continue. KEEP UP WITH = match someone's progress. KEEP DOWN = control / suppress (anger, voice). All common SSC, banking, CGL phrasals.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'PUT UP WITH': 'I cannot put up with this noise any longer.'
questions.explanation: PUT UP WITH = tolerate, endure (something unpleasant). 3-part phrasal verb (rare). 'Put up with the boss's tantrums.' Other PUT phrasals: PUT OFF = postpone; PUT ON = wear / pretend; PUT OUT = extinguish (fire) / annoy; PUT AWAY = store; PUT DOWN = criticize / set down; PUT UP = host / accommodate / display.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'LET DOWN': 'He really let me down by not coming.'
questions.explanation: LET (someone) DOWN = disappoint; fail to meet expectations. 'Don't let me down!' Famous song by Beatles + Daft Punk. LET phrasals: LET OFF = excuse / release / discharge (let off the hook = excuse from blame); LET IN = allow inside; LET OUT = release / make wider / leak out; LET UP = decrease / pause (e.g., 'rain didn't let up').
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'CARRY OUT': 'The team will carry out the survey next week.'
questions.explanation: CARRY OUT = perform, execute, conduct. 'Carry out orders, instructions, an investigation, an experiment.' CARRY phrasals: CARRY ON = continue; CARRY OFF = succeed at / achieve (also win a prize); CARRY OVER = transfer to next period; CARRY THROUGH = complete (esp. through difficulty); CARRY AWAY = excite emotionally ('got carried away').
